type:
∀ (R S : Type u) [Ring R] [Ring S],
  (∀ (F : CategoryTheory.Functor (ModuleCat.{u} R) (ModuleCat.{u} S))
    [CategoryTheory.Functor.Additive F],
    NotesProofs.WattsPreservesCokernels F →
    NotesProofs.WattsPreservesCoproducts F →
    CategoryTheory.IsIso (NotesProofs.wattsComparisonNatTrans F)) ∧
  (∀ (B : Type u) [AddCommGroup B] [Module S B] [Module (MulOpposite R) B]
    [SMulCommClass (MulOpposite R) S B],
    let T := NotesProofs.concreteTensorFunctor (R := R) (S := S) B
    CategoryTheory.Functor.Additive T ∧
      NotesProofs.WattsPreservesCokernels T ∧
      NotesProofs.WattsPreservesCoproducts T)

The cached TeX and PDF agree on Ian X, Abelian Categories and Bimodules, Theorem 9.4 (env-9-4, p. 30), with the functor hypotheses from Definition 9.1 and the regular action and canonical comparison from Lemmas 9.2–9.3. The published PDF matches the cached PDF byte for byte. https://getcurious.cc/downloads/abelian-categories-and-bimodules-lecture-notes.pdf#page=30

The owner’s input.request confirms the notes’ ordinary-choice convention and permits propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. The Lean family uses one arbitrary ambient universe for rings, modules, and indexing sets. It covers arbitrary associative unital rings, including the zero ring, and unital left modules. Right exactness means preservation of cokernels, and coproduct preservation ranges over every index type in the ambient universe, including the empty type. IsIso applies to the specified natural transformation τ^F from tensoring by F of the lifted left regular module to F. Its right action comes from F applied to right multiplication, and its component sends b ⊗ m to F(λ_m)(b). The other direction uses the concrete tensor functor of each bimodule, with the right action encoded as a commuting left action of MulOpposite R. The shared-slot Lean check of the exact type used the compiled NotesProofs.ConcreteTensorPreservation and reported exactly the three permitted axioms.
